narrative.title: Counting the Landlocked Plots
narrative.scenario: A harbour authority maps its estate as a grid of dock-access plots (1) and sealed lots (0). A plot grants an exit if a worker can walk across adjacent plots to the estate boundary and step off. The audit wants the number of plots from which no such walk exists — the fully landlocked ones, however large their inland cluster is.
narrative.inputFormat: An m x n binary matrix grid where 0 is a sealed lot and 1 is a dock-access plot.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the number of land cells from which the grid boundary cannot be reached by 4-directional moves.

testCases.explanation: The three inland plots form one cluster sealed off by lots on every side.
Both plots sit on the boundary — each can step straight off the estate.

hintLevels: Level 1: Mirror of Surrounded Regions — eliminate everything with a border escape, then count the rest.
Level 2: Flood from every land cell on the perimeter; whatever stays unvisited is landlocked.
Level 3: The final count is a plain tally over unvisited land — no per-cluster bookkeeping.
